title: Approver Heatstrip — Compact approver-impact timeline with cost deltas
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem:
Teams using Redwood Console need a compact way to evaluate who will be affected by role changes and what the short-term cost/throughput impact will be. Current audit timeline views are wide, verbose, and separate from cost telemetry; this forces admins to switch contexts when deciding whether to approve role changes or schedule rollouts.

Proposal summary:
Design a small, scannable component called the 'Approver Heatstrip' that sits inside the access review and role-edit flows. It shows a horizontal, time-aligned micro-timeline per approver or role group with three overlaid layers: (1) density of expected affected requests (heat), (2) estimated cost delta band (low/medium/high), and (3) rollout windows and active approvals. Interactions include hover-to-expand for audit snippets, one-click 'simulate rollout' that invokes a backend evaluation API, and inline justifications pulled from recent audit comments.

Key UX goals:
- Let reviewers triage approvals without leaving the role editor or audit list.
- Surface cost implications early (token-level cost + throughput risk) so PMs can weigh trade-offs before enabling permissions.
- Keep the component compact (fits a single audit list row) while providing deep-dive affordances (popover / secondary panel).

Design trade-offs considered:
- Compactness vs. fidelity: we biased toward a simplified heat density and three-tier cost band to avoid cognitive overload. Exact dollar values are available on click to avoid cluttering the primary view.
- Live cost estimates vs. cached snapshots: initial MVP will show a cached 24h projection (fast and deterministic). Later iterations will toggle to live recalculation for high-confidence enterprise installs.
- Permissions sensitivity: audit snippets are truncated; full details respect workspace RBAC and will open only for users with ‘view audit details’ privilege.

Prototypes and artifacts:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/REDWOOD/approver-heatstrip-mvp (frames: compact-list, popover-detail, simulate-workflow)
- Clickable prototype: https://redwood-proto.app/heatstrip/preview
- Confluence PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONSOLE/pages/Heatstrip+Design+Spec
- Evaluation API RFC (internal): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/u/0/folders/heatstrip-rfc
- Example GH backend branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2387

Acceptance criteria (see list below):
- Heatstrip appears on each access-review row for workspaces with audit-enabled flag.
- Hover reveals truncated audit snippet and last approver comment.
- Clicking 'Simulate' calls the evaluation endpoint and displays a 24h projected cost delta and request impact score.
- Users without audit access see a greyed state with 'insufficient permissions' tooltip.
- Usability testing (N=8) yields median SUS >= 75 for task: 'decide whether to approve role change'.
acceptance_criteria: Component renders in audit list and role editor rows
Hover popover shows recent audit snippets and justification
Simulate button triggers evaluation API and displays cost delta band
Permission gating respects RBAC and hides details when unauthorized
Performance: initial render latency < 120ms in list view (mocked)
comments: 2026-02-26 - Aisha Kumar: Initial draft uploaded to Figma and PRD. Added simulation API contract to RFC. Seeking alignment on cost-bands (token vs. dollar).
2026-03-02 - PM review (Diego Morales): Liked compact approach. Request: surface 'affected services' tag alongside heatstrip to help SREs triage risk. Added as follow-up.

2026-03-04 - Eng feedback (Maya Chen): Suggested we reuse existing evaluation endpoint (ENG-22411) and return a deterministic 24h snapshot to avoid rate limits. Also noted backend needs a lightweight cache layer. Marked as dependency.
2026-03-08 - Design critique: Usability team recommended increasing touch targets for popover on mobile and adding keyboard navigation for accessibility. Added changes to prototype.
2026-03-10 - Security review (R. Singh): Confirmed no additional PII exposed by truncated audit snippets; full audit details will remain behind existing RBAC checks. Security review cleared for MVP.
usability_plan: Moderated remote sessions with 8 participants across admin/PM/SRE roles. Tasks: triage a pending approval, run simulate, interpret cost delta, schedule rollout. Sessions planned 2026-03-14 to 2026-03-16.
next_steps: Address engineering notes about caching and API rate limits, finalize Figma frames for dev handoff, run first round of usability tests, update PRD with test outcomes, schedule handoff ticket to ENG-UI (ENG-24618).
notes: Avoid numeric cost precision in the primary view to prevent false confidence. Use bands and confidence level (low/med/high) plus link to detailed breakdown. Consider future integration with Optimize suggestions for quantization or batching to reduce projected delta.
